subject: General Knowledge
description: Firsts, Dadasaheb Phalke, Oscars, film industries

questions.stem: India's first full-length feature film, 'Raja Harishchandra' (1913), was directed by:
questions.explanation: Dhundiraj Govind Phalke ('Dadasaheb Phalke') directed 'Raja Harishchandra' — released 3 May 1913 at Coronation Cinematograph, Bombay. He is called the 'Father of Indian Cinema'. The Dadasaheb Phalke Award (instituted 1969) is the highest Indian film honour. Satyajit Ray (Pather Panchali 1955, Apu Trilogy) — India's most famous art-cinema director; awarded a lifetime Oscar in 1992.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.explanation: 'Alam Ara' (1931), directed by Ardeshir Irani, was India's first sound / talkie film. Its songs (composed by Firozshah Mistry and B. Irani) marked the beginning of the Indian film-song tradition. Raja Harishchandra was silent (1913). Devdas has been made multiple times (1935 P. C. Barua, 1955 Bimal Roy, 2002 Sanjay Leela Bhansali). Mother India (1957) was India's first Oscar nomination for Best Foreign-Language Film.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Satyajit Ray was awarded an honorary Lifetime Achievement Oscar in:
questions.explanation: Satyajit Ray received the Lifetime Achievement Oscar at the 64th Academy Awards (March 1992) — the first Indian to win this honour. He was too ill to travel; received the award in hospital just weeks before his death in April 1992. India won its first competitive Oscar for 'Slumdog Millionaire' (2008) in the Music (AR Rahman) and Song (Jai Ho) categories; 'RRR' — Naatu Naatu — won Best Original Song in 2023.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Match the film industry with its city / region. A. Bollywood. B. Tollywood (Telugu). C. Kollywood. D. Mollywood. List-II: 1. Mumbai, 2. Hyderabad, 3. Chennai, 4. Kerala (Malayalam cinema).
questions.explanation: Bollywood — Hindi cinema, Mumbai (was 'Bombay Talkies'). Tollywood — Telugu cinema, Hyderabad (and earlier, Tollygunge, Kolkata was the origin of the 'T' suffix for the Bengali industry). Kollywood — Tamil cinema, Chennai / Kodambakkam. Mollywood — Malayalam cinema, Kerala. Sandalwood — Kannada cinema, Bengaluru. India makes the largest number of feature films in the world annually (~1,500-2,000).

questions.stem: The 100th Indian Science Congress (2013) was inaugurated by the then Prime Minister — but the 'Dadasaheb Phalke Award' was instituted in:
questions.explanation: The Dadasaheb Phalke Award was instituted in 1969 on Phalke's birth centenary. First recipient — actress Devika Rani (1969). Other early recipients — Birendranath Sircar, Prithviraj Kapoor. Recent honours have gone to Waheeda Rehman (2021). The award carries a Swarna Kamal (Golden Lotus), a shawl and a cash prize (currently ₹10 lakh). Administered by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting through the Directorate of Film Festivals.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: 'Mother India' (1957) — India's first Oscar-nominated feature for Best Foreign-Language Film — was directed by:
questions.explanation: Mehboob Khan directed Mother India (1957), starring Nargis. Nominated for the Best Foreign-Language Oscar at the 30th Academy Awards; lost by a single vote to Federico Fellini's 'Nights of Cabiria'. Raj Kapoor — 'Awaara' (1951), 'Shree 420' (1955). Bimal Roy — 'Do Bigha Zameen' (1953), 'Madhumati' (1958). Guru Dutt — 'Pyaasa' (1957), 'Kaagaz Ke Phool' (1959).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The only Indian documentary to win an Oscar (2023 — 'The Elephant Whisperers') was directed by:
questions.explanation: Kartiki Gonsalves directed 'The Elephant Whisperers' — which won the Best Documentary Short Film Oscar at the 95th Academy Awards (March 2023). Guneet Monga was the producer. The film tells the story of a tribal couple in Tamil Nadu caring for the orphan elephant Raghu. At the same ceremony, 'Naatu Naatu' from 'RRR' won Best Original Song (composer M. M. Keeravani, lyricist Chandrabose).
